rationale: Evidence from iteration 3 (score 697.4, best so far): the oval (20/20, 1.84 s, rms 0.007) and s-bend (20/20, 2.08 s, rms 0.016) both finish cleanly. The slalom is the only failure: 20/20 off-track exits at mean progress 0.48, with one line-loss event per run and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 3 changed kp 3.0 to 3.5, kd 1.4 to 1.6, and sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016. Slalom progress rose from 0.26 to 0.48, which supports the view that slalom exits come from losing the tape at direction reversals and from insufficient steering authority. Steering oscillation on the slalom rose to 0.27, which means the higher kp is starting to add some jitter. Changes: (1) kp 3.5 to 4.0 for more steering authority on the sharp slalom reversals. (2) kd 1.6 to 2.0 to keep the damping ratio in line with the higher kp and to limit the jitter that rose in iteration 3. (3) Sensor spread widened from x = +/-0.05 to +/-0.06 m (still at y = 0.07 m, inside the allowed limit). Outer sensors then see the tape earlier on the sharp reversals, which should reduce line-loss events. Sensor weights are unchanged, so the signal stays bounded within +/-1. base_speed 1.2, ki 0.02, mass 0.6, wheel geometry and sensor_size 0.016 are kept unchanged, so the effect of the steering and sensor-spread changes can be read directly. Expected result: slalom progress rising above 0.6 with line_loss_events falling toward 0.5 per run, while the oval and s-bend keep their finishes. The risk is that kp 4.0 brings back the oscillation seen in iteration 0, so the oscillation metric is the first thing to check. Hypotheses: (a) line-loss exits on the slalom are caused by outer sensors seeing no tape at the reversals, so the wider spread should cut line losses; (b) kd 2.0 is enough to hold steering oscillation near 0.2 at kp 4.0. Measurements I want next: per-track progress and completion, line_loss_events per track, steering_oscillation on the slalom, max_error location, and completion_time on the oval and s-bend, to check whether speed or steering is the limit.
